answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a bonded-work ledger: every new agent must escrow a stake proportional to the voting weight it claims, and that stake is slashed whenever its output fails random peer re-execution. A puppet identity therefore costs real capital before it earns a single vote, so a thousand sybils need a thousand simultaneous bonds, each exposed to loss. Reputation accrues only through attested work, slowly, like juniper rooting into a canyon wall, while the eligibility rules stay basalt: fixed, unyielding, identical for everyone.
